headline: A 2016 law directs the Architect of the Capitol to place a chair honoring prisoners of war and missing service members in the Capitol, paid for with private donations.
what_it_does: The law tells the Architect of the Capitol to obtain a chair that bears the logo of the National League of POW/MIA Families and to put it in a suitable permanent spot in the U.S. Capitol within two years. The Architect may work with tax-exempt charities to collect private donations for this purpose and may accept donated money, property, or services. All costs must be covered by those private donations.
when_it_takes_effect: The chair was to be placed within two years after the law was enacted on April 29, 2016.
